text:
I found ACME's "Brand mentions" monitor (id 501) and pulled its daily trend data for the requested window (2026-06-01 through 2026-06-28), which returned all 28 days with `sentiment_score` values (documented in the API schema as a 0–100 scale where 0 = negative and 100 = positive, so a score above the 50 midpoint represents net-positive sentiment for that day).

Counting days where `sentiment_score` > 50 (net positive):
- 06-02 (76), 06-03 (76), 06-05 (52), 06-06 (60), 06-07 (74), 06-08 (80), 06-09 (75), 06-13 (76), 06-15 (77), 06-16 (83), 06-19 (60), 06-21 (70), 06-23 (84), 06-24 (65), 06-26 (77)

That's 15 days out of the 28-day window. (Days at exactly 50, e.g. 06-11 and 06-27, were treated as neutral, not positive, per the scale's midpoint.)

Note: I found no explicit ACME business-rule definition of "positive coverage" in the knowledge base or memory beyond the API's own documented sentiment scale, so this count relies on the natural midpoint (>50) of that documented 0–100 scale.

FINAL ANSWER: 15
